correctness.rationale: From L(u)/b=alpha*u/(1+u²)+r*u/(1+r²u²), derivative sign is cubic P(Y)=alpha(1-Y)(1+r²Y)²+r(1-r²Y)(1+Y)². Positive stationary points lie in 1/r²<Y<1. Solving P=P'=0 with y=u²,z=r²u² eliminates alpha and gives z=(3-y)/(1-3y), A(y) and R(y) for 0<y<1/3. The derivative of log A is -3(y²-6y+1)²/[2y(3-y)(1-y)(1+y)(1-3y)], hence unique threshold per alpha; root continuation gives one vs two maxima, and triple-root symmetry gives quartically flat center. Exact Taylor expansion yields the 2/3 cusp and r_*(alpha)~8max(alpha,alpha^-1). Independently evaluated the older published exact reciprocal wedge at five strength ratios; its thresholds match the new curve, and its cusp converts to K=6.181980515339463 precisely. Finite comparisons corroborate proof, not generality.
